CiteRef.description: Forward citation edge; ``label`` resolves in the CND ``bibliography`` pool.
CiteRef.title: CiteRef

DeclBibEntry.description:
A bibliography entry in a declaration — ``BibEntry`` minus ``id``.

The content floor still applies at build time: an entry must carry
``formatted``, a structured field, or both. It is a builder check, not
a shape the schema expresses.
DeclBibEntry.title: DeclBibEntry

DeclCell.description: One cell of a declared ``table`` or ``layout``; content is nodes.
DeclCell.title: DeclCell

DeclFigureNode.description:
A captioned wrapper. Keeps ``kind`` (the category, and the counter
the engine draws from) and ``numbering.name`` (authored for a custom
``kind`` the builder has no localized word for).
DeclFigureNode.title: DeclFigureNode

DeclFootnote.description:
A footnote in a declaration — ``Footnote`` minus ``id``. Its content
is nodes, which the builder mints ids for like any other node.
DeclFootnote.title: DeclFootnote

DeclHeadingNode.description:
A section heading. No ``heading_path`` (derivable from tree
position) and no resolved number.

``level`` starts at 1 — there is no level 0. Constraining it here
makes the invalid input unrepresentable rather than a counter-engine
crash at build time (ADR 0019 §4's own philosophy: reject at the
door, not downstream).
DeclHeadingNode.title: DeclHeadingNode

DeclListItem.description:
One item of a declaration list; its content is nodes.

``number`` is an **override**, not a resolved ordinal: absent means
"number this item sequentially", present means an explicit start or
skip (markdown's ``3.`` on the first item of an ordered list). It keeps
the *authored* half (the override) and drops the *derived* half (the
running ordinal), the same line drawn for ``numbering``.

Resolution rule the builder follows (pinned so two builders cannot
diverge): an item with no ``number`` takes the previous sibling's
resolved number plus one, starting from 1; an item *with* a ``number``
takes it verbatim, and following items count on from there. So a
``number`` **rebases** the rest of the list rather than only labelling
its own item. Ignored on an ``ordered: false`` list, which has no
ordinals. A nested list is a ``list`` node among the children and
counts on its own.
DeclListItem.title: DeclListItem

DeclNumbering.description:
The authored half of ``Numbering``: the counter word alone.

Present means "this element carries this word" ("Listing",
"Théorème"); the builder's counter engine supplies the value. There is
no ``value`` field, so a declaration cannot carry one.
DeclNumbering.title: DeclNumbering

DeclTableNode.description:
``kind`` is the author's statement (``"data"``, ``"content"``, or
any other value of the open vocabulary); the builder never guesses
one.
DeclTableNode.title: DeclTableNode

DocDate.description: Partial or full document date from cnd metadata.
DocDate.title: DocDate

DocMetadata.description:
Bibliographic metadata for the work the CND represents.

This identifies the *work* — title, authors, date. The input artifact it
was built from is ``Cnd.source``, deliberately separate: the same work
can be built from a Typst source and later re-imported from another
format (docs/proposals/0008).

``status`` and ``version`` are the values the author declares on the
document, unrelated to ``cnd_version`` and to any build history. ``extra``
holds any other title-page metadata; its keys never repeat a field name
(validation, docs/proposals/0013).
DocMetadata.title: DocMetadata

FootnoteRef.description: Forward footnote edge; ``label`` resolves in the CND ``footnotes`` pool.
FootnoteRef.title: FootnoteRef

LinkRef.description:
Forward hyperlink edge; ``href`` resolves nowhere in the CND.

The fourth forward family and the only one not keyed by label: a
hyperlink's target is outside the document by definition, so it admits
no resolution domain and has no dangling state — a URL is a URL. The
scheme is a consumer's business (``https:``, ``doi:``, an application
scheme); the format only carries the string.
LinkRef.title: LinkRef

Mark.description:
A standoff span of inline formatting inside a ``RichText.value``.

``raw`` is the source of the covered text, used by ``math`` (the
readable linear form lives in ``value``, the formula here).
Mark.title: Mark

NodeRef.description:
Forward cross-reference edge to another node.

An edge is ``{label, text_span?}``: it names its target by label and
resolves through the CND's label index (docs/adr/0017, superseding the
``{id, label}`` form of docs/adr/0002). ``text_span`` marks where the
reference marker sits in the ``value`` of the ``RichText`` that holds
the edge, as a ``[start, end)`` pair of Unicode code-point offsets
(docs/adr/0013).
NodeRef.title: NodeRef

RawSource.description:
The producer's verbatim source for a node, with its language.

A bare string dropped the one thing a consumer needs to decide whether
to attempt a parse: which language the content is in. ``format`` is an
open string (``"typst"``, ``"latex"``, ``"mathml"``…), never a closed
enum — a new producer must not require a spec revision.
RawSource.title: RawSource

RichText.description:
Prose: a text, its language, its marks and its forward edges.

An edge belongs to the text in which its marker opens; its owning
node is the nearest node holding the text. Every list defaults to
empty and may be omitted, so ``{"value": "…"}`` is a complete text.
``lang`` null inherits from the enclosing text, then the node chain,
then ``doc.lang``.
RichText.title: RichText

SourceInfo.description:
The input artifact the CND was built from.

``hash`` is self-describing (``"sha256:…"``). Its comparability is
narrow and normative: two hashes are comparable only between CNDs from
the **same producer over the same source**, where equal means unchanged
and different means changed. Comparing across producers is meaningless.

``uri`` is an identifier in the producer's own space and is **never
promised resolvable** — a consumer must not dereference it.
SourceInfo.title: SourceInfo

description:
The source form a producer emits and the builder compiles.

No ``id``, ``built_at`` or ``cnd_version`` — all three are the
builder's to supply. ``source`` is kept, optional: a producer
converting ``notes.md`` legitimately records what it converted from,
and provenance is not resolved presentation state.

``declaration_version`` is **required**, matching the CND's required
``cnd_version``. It exists to stop the first evolution of the schema
from breaking every producer silently (ADR 0019 §3); an omitted
version defaulting to "current" is exactly the silent assumption it
guards against, so absence is an error, not "latest".
title: CND declaration
